title: Using machine learning to predict future foster care admission.
ehr_evidence: We make use of data from CareSource Ohio, a nonprofit health plan with the largest Medicaid enrollment in the state of Ohio.
summary: A predictive modeling study using Medicaid claims data for children under 18 enrolled in a Ohio health plan to compare gradient-boosted tree and logistic regression performance in predicting future foster care admission.
key_findings: Using a gradient-boosted tree algorithm, 2408 children (1.32%) were identified as at risk of foster care admission in a sample of 181 841, of whom 1599 entered foster care within 1 year, yielding a PPV of 66.4% (F1 = 55.5%, specificity = 99.5%, sensitivity = 47.67%).
Accuracy was substantially better when using SDOH data (PPV of 84.72% with SDOH data compared to 27.44% without).
The gradient-boosted tree substantially outperformed logistic regression; without SDOH variables logistic regression yielded a PPV of 0%, and with SDOH variables a PPV of 12.7%.
Average Precision was 0.75 for the SDOH model and 0.16 for the non-SDOH model.
captured_features: Clinical diagnoses and healthcare utilization of children
Diagnoses and utilization of linked parental adults
Johns Hopkins ACG System health analytics scores
21 SDOH risk scores (geographic/contextual and household-level socioeconomic factors such as education spending, household liens, bankruptcies, evictions, and criminal justice involvement)
population: Children under 18 years enrolled in CareSource's Ohio Medicaid plan, January 2019 through June 2022
limitations: Some prior or future foster care admissions may be missing from the data or due to enrollment with a different health plan.
The model was trained on a single health plan population and may not generalize to demographically and clinically distinct populations.
No information on sibling status, preventing control for household clustering across training and validation sets.
